# Green Basket grocer

Generated by Upskale Studio from your Flux sources. Edit the project in
Studio and download it again rather than editing `lib/` by hand — the next
download replaces it.

## Run it

This download contains the app (`lib/`) and its `pubspec.yaml`. Flutter
creates the platform folders for you, once:

```sh
flutter create . --project-name green_basket_grocer --platforms=android,ios,web
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

`flutter create .` only adds what is missing (`android/`, `ios/`, `web/`…)
and leaves `lib/` and `pubspec.yaml` as they are. Choose the platforms you
need; `--platforms=android` alone is enough for an APK:

```sh
flutter build apk
```

The app loads images and its typeface (Plus Jakarta Sans, through
`google_fonts`) over the network. Debug builds can already do that; for a
release build on Android, add this line inside `<manifest>` in
`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
```

## What's inside

- `lib/main.dart` — the app and a route for each page.
- `lib/pages/` — one widget per page.
- `lib/components/` — your reusable components.
- `lib/studio_runtime.dart` — the small helper library the generated widgets use.
- `lib/studio_generated.dart` — exports everything above.

Stores, menus, location search and the cart come from
[`upskale_storefront`](https://github.com/iamsinyagepr/storefront-sdk-flutter), the tenant API
client every generated app installs. `lib/main.dart` points it at your
instance's API with `Storefront.configure(apiBaseUrl: ...)`. To replace a
control with your own, pass a `StudioPlatform` in a page's
`bindings['_studio']` (see `lib/studio_runtime.dart`).
